acceptanceCriteria: Limit production changes to cockpit-git bounded committed-source snapshot generation and a private v1 patch metadata canonicalizer. Add one independent regression target. In the existing bounded_source_comparison_preserves_existing_hunk_facts test only, explicitly configure its local Git fixture with core.abbrev=8 and assert configuration success for the declared legacy-v1 compatibility comparison. Keep every existing assertion unchanged. No dependencies, other Work Items, archived Contract bytes, frozen receipts, or existing four historical test assertions are changed.

For the explicitly supported legacy v1 SHA-1 source patch recipe evidenced by the frozen WI-1078 request, changing core.abbrev, adding unrelated Git objects, or creating an eight-character blob prefix collision does not change the committed source patch identity. Eight-character display metadata never becomes content authority: complete blob IDs and source content bindings remain intact, and changing tracked bytes remains distinguishable.

Normalize only real textual diff metadata headers. Preserve index-like or binary-marker-like text inside hunks, binary patch full object IDs and payload, added/deleted zero IDs, and mode/rename semantics under the existing no-renames route. Unsupported hash algorithms, malformed or unsupported metadata must fail explicitly rather than inventing a compatible historical identity.

Retain bounded Git output reading before canonicalization. A full-index patch that exceeds the input budget must return the existing bounded-output failure and cannot be truncated into a complete passing digest.

First run cargo test --locked -p cockpit-git --test source_patch_identity as an authorized red regression against unchanged production code, preserving its true failure output; implement only after a behavioral red. Green validation covers the real Git cases above, all cockpit-git package tests, and the four unchanged historical post-merge tests with their original frozen golden records.

Run the declared local checks with actual commands and exit codes. The four repository targets use --release to reuse an isolated copy of existing build artifacts; this does not claim workspace, Windows, or fresh provider CI passed. All original CI failure logs and reconstruction provenance remain available.

After implementation and independent review, use normal Runtime-supported provider binding and real strict CI before any integration. PR 1052 remains unmerged while its requirements are unmet. No new authority platform, B implementation, external credentials or permissions, release, forced push, historical debt clearing, or cleanup of unrelated resources is authorized by this Work Item.
